In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
a single stuck fault set is not always a multiple stuck fault set in multi-output circuits.

a single stuck fault (SSF) test set for a multi-output irredundant circuit is a multiple stuck fault (MSF) test set for all multiple faults in the circuit, if and only if, for each output function, the variables are ordered in such a way that the output function is irredundant with respect to each variable.

a single stuck fault set will detect all single and multiple faults in a two-level multi-output circuit if and only if it satisfies the following two constraints: (a) the circuit is irredundant; and (b) each output function is irredundantly prime.
